methodology:
Compare digest-checked archived SKILL.md bytes with fixed upstream branch heads.

Deterministic primary order: adds_execution > adds_network > widens_permissions >
changes_code_examples > instructions_changed > cosmetic. Execution means a new
download-and-run, package installer (npx/uvx/pip install), interpreter-script, or
./script command. A new/edited executable-language fence without a new command
is a code-example signal, subordinate to network and permission changes.
All matching signals remain in flags. Compare
whitespace-normalized blocks/commands as sets, not individual diff lines. Network
means a new HTTP(S) URL (including a new URL on an existing domain); report new
hostnames separately (localhost and loopback URLs are excluded). Permission fields named allowed-tools, tools, tool,
permissions or permission, at any frontmatter depth, widen when their flattened
values gain tokens; false/null values grant no tokens. This is a textual
heuristic, not permission semantics.
Instructions means >6 added+removed nonempty body lines after removing whitespace
and Markdown formatting characters; all remaining edits are cosmetic, including
potentially meaningful tiny edits and currently identical bytes (flagged
identical_bytes). Raw added/removed line counts are also stored.

Closed executable fences: sh, bash, shell, zsh, console, terminal, python,
python3, py, javascript, js, typescript, ts, powershell, ps1, ruby, perl, php,
go, rust, c, cpp, sql. An edit within an existing executable block counts as
a new block if its whitespace-normalized contents differ. Shell backslash-newline
continuations are joined for command matching. Download-and-run matches curl/wget
piped to sh/bash/python; interpreter-script matches python/bash/sh/node/ruby/perl
with a .py/.sh/.js/.mjs/.rb/.pl path; ./ commands accept extensionless names or
.sh/.py/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.rb/.pl/.ps1. Plain text/JSON/YAML fences are not execution
signals by themselves. Body normalization removes whitespace and `*_#>|~-;
other punctuation and letter case remain significant. YAML permission tokens
are split on whitespace/commas, keeping mapping paths and ignoring list order.
Non-permission frontmatter changes do not contribute to the body-line threshold.
If the concatenated normalized body lines are identical, reflow alone contributes
zero changed body lines.

Not a safety verdict: examples, documentation and modified existing code blocks
can trigger flags; unfenced code, prose permissions and non-HTTP links can escape
them. No code is executed. Only SKILL.md is compared, not bundled assets. A path
404 triggers a recursive tree lookup at the same commit. A replacement SKILL.md
matches if its parent directory equals the archived directory name, or its YAML
frontmatter name equals the archived frontmatter name. Directory matches take
precedence; ties use the lexicographically first path. Moved files retain their
normal content classification in moved_change_class. No match in a complete
search means removed. Failed/truncated trees or incomplete name searches mean
path_missing_unchecked, never assumed removal. Other comparison failures are
fetch_failed. Evidence contains only raw added lines, at most four per snippet.
The unavailable cohort is rechecked: head 404 + repository 404 => repo_404
(includes private/inaccessible repos); head 404 + accessible repo =>
branch_not_found; other failures => other; recovered heads => available_now.
If metadata lacks a branch, only repository availability is checked: a 404 is
repo_404, an accessible repository is other (branch unknown). Source-path metadata
defects do not prevent checking repository/branch availability.

Cache fixes the data main SHA and each upstream head on first successful fetch;
reuse the same directory to resume that observation, a fresh directory to refresh.
Successful responses and 404s are cached; transient errors are retried twice
and never cached. 403/429 are reported explicitly, without retry storms. Every
selected pin produces a row; fetch_failed/unchecked/other make the command exit
nonzero. --cache-only makes no network requests. Authentication comes only from
GITHUB_TOKEN when set; no CLI credential lookup is performed.

evidence:
- Creating durable handoff summaries that preserve decisions, files, risks, and next actions

Do not activate this skill for adjacent work owned by other skills:
- General token-efficiency tactics such as masking, prefix caching, or partitioning: `context-optimization`.
Context compression trades token savings against information loss. Select from three production-ready approaches based on session characteristics:

1. **Anchored Iterative Summarization**: Implement this for long-running sessions where file tracking matters. Maintain structured, persistent summaries with explicit sections for session intent, file modifications, decisions, and next steps. When compression triggers, summarize only the newly-truncated span and merge with the existing summary rather than regenerating from scratch. This prevents drift that accumulates when summaries are regenerated wholesale — each regeneration risks losing details the model considers low-priority but the task requires. Structure forces preservation because dedicated sections act as checklists the summarizer must populate, catching silent information loss.
### Optimize for Tokens-Per-Task, Not Tokens-Per-Request

Measure total tokens consumed from task start to completion, not tokens per individual request. When compression drops file paths, error messages, or decision rationale, the agent must re-explore, re-read files, and re-derive conclusions — wasting far more tokens than the compression saved. A strategy saving 0.5% more tokens per request but causing 20% more re-fetching costs more overall. Track re-fetching frequency as the primary quality signal: if the agent repeatedly asks to re-read files it already processed, compression is too aggressive.
skills.name: context-compression

1. **Labels, not prose.** A screen is label → value → action; the label carries the meaning (`Batch savings (7d)`). If a number needs a paragraph, rename it; if it still needs a definition, one sentence in a tooltip. No page or section descriptions on dashboard and functionality pages: a title is not followed by a sentence. Moving one into a help icon is a fix, never a regression, and lost taglines are not damage. AI-written descriptions are worse than none ("Choose which channels each notice reaches you on…"). Only promotional pages may carry one.
2. **A dashboard is numbers, lists and tables**. Per signal: title, number, share, a compact table of top rows; no "meaning" text, threshold sentences or hints under tiles. One big table first, drill-downs beneath it or on click, never scattered panels each with its own story. A broken dashboard is fixed surgically, keeping what worked (the window picker, the dimensions, the drill); never rip data out to undo a mistake. The hooks compute a SHA-256 of `task_plan.md` on every fire and compare against the stored hash. On mismatch, injection is blocked with a `[PLAN TAMPERED]` warning. This detects a plan-only change while the saved digest remains trusted. The digest is an ordinary local SHA-256 value, not a keyed signature: a process that can replace both the plan and the attestation can make new content pass. Auto-attestation during initialization records the generated bytes; it is not proof of human review. Attestation does not make embedded instructions trustworthy or eliminate model-level prompt injection.

The attestation is written to `.planning/<active-plan>/.attestation` (parallel-plan mode) or `./.plan-attestation` (legacy mode). When set, the injected context also carries a `Plan-SHA256:` line so the model can log the attested hash for audit.

evidence: Diagnose and fix context failures before they cascade. Context degradation is not binary — it is a continuum that manifests through five distinct, predictable patterns: lost-in-middle, poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash. Each pattern has specific detection signals and mitigation strategies. Treat degradation as an engineering problem with measurable thresholds, not an unpredictable failure mode.

Do not activate this skill for adjacent work owned by other skills:
- Explaining foundational context mechanics without an active failure: `context-fundamentals`.
- Applying token-efficiency tactics after the failure pattern is known: `context-optimization`.
- Designing a compression or handoff summary strategy: `context-compression`.

Structure context placement around the attention U-curve: beginning and end positions receive reliable attention, while middle positions suffer materially reduced recall accuracy in long-context experiments (claim-context-degradation-lost-middle-ruler). This is not a model bug but a consequence of attention mechanics — the first token (often BOS) acts as an "attention sink" that absorbs disproportionate attention budget, leaving middle tokens under-attended as context grows.

Treat context poisoning as a circuit breaker problem. Once a hallucination, tool error, or incorrect retrieved fact enters context, it compounds through repeated self-reference. A poisoned goals section causes every downstream decision to reinforce incorrect assumptions. Detection requires tracking claim provenance; recovery requires truncating to before the poisoning point or restarting with verified-only context.

evidence:
Design every tool as a contract between a deterministic system and a non-deterministic agent. Unlike human-facing APIs, agent-facing tools must make the contract unambiguous through the description alone: agents infer intent from descriptions and generate calls that must match expected formats. Every ambiguity becomes a potential failure mode that no amount of prompt engineering can fix.

The unit of work for this skill is a single tool or a tool catalog. Project-shape, pipeline architecture, task-model-fit, and cost-at-the-project-level decisions belong to `project-development`. Deciding whether to introduce sub-agents belongs to `multi-agent-patterns`. This skill owns the interface layer that connects deterministic code to the agent.

Activate this skill when the unit of work is a tool:

- Writing a new tool description, schema, or response format.
- Debugging cases where the agent picked the wrong tool or generated malformed calls.

Design tools around the consolidation principle: if a human engineer cannot definitively say which tool should be used in a given situation, an agent cannot be expected to do better. Reduce the tool set until each tool has one unambiguous purpose, because agents select tools by comparing descriptions and any overlap introduces selection errors.

Treat every tool description as prompt engineering that shapes agent behavior. The description is not documentation for humans -- it is injected into the agent's context and directly steers reasoning. Write descriptions that answer what the tool does, when to use it, and what it returns, because these three questions are exactly what agents evaluate during tool selection.
